Othello Hunter''' (born May 28, 1986) is an American-Liberian[http://www.menssanabasket.it/en/giocatori/othello-hunter/ MensSanaBasket.it Othello Hunter.] former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=8}}, he played at the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. Hunter played four seasons of [[college basketball]] including two seasons for [[Hillsborough Community College|Hillsborough CC]] and two seasons for [[Ohio State University]]. [[File:Othello Hunter 44 PBC CSKA Moscow 20171027 (cropped).jpg|thumb|200px|Othello Hunter in 2017]] ==High school career== Hunter attended [[Richard J. Reynolds High School]], in his hometown of [[Winston-Salem]], [[North Carolina]] where he played high school basketball.{{Cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Othello-Hunter-5024/|title=DraftExpress - Othello Hunter DraftExpress Profile: Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook|website=DraftExpress|language=en|access-date=2018-05-03|archive-date=October 15, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141015101726/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Othello-Hunter-5024/|url-status=dead}} ==College career== After high school, Hunter attended [[Hillsborough Community College]], in [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]], [[Hillsborough County, Florida|Hillsborough County, FL]] for two years, and he became a part of the [[Ohio State University]]'s 2006 "Thad Five" recruiting class. After playing two seasons at Ohio State University, with the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Buckeyes]], during which he managed to post the seventh-best single-season field-goal percentage in school history, he entered the [[2008 NBA draft]], in which he was not selected. ==Professional career== ===NBA=== Hunter joined the [[Atlanta Hawks]]' summer league squad in the summer of 2008. In five summer league games, he posted 13.2 points per game, 2.0 assists per game, 1.2 steals per game, and led his team with 6.2 rebounds per game. On August 11, 2008, the Hawks announced that they had signed Hunter to a contract.[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Hawks_Sign_Hunter_Gardner_081108.html Hawks Sign Hunter, Gardner], August 11, 2008 Hunter was waived by the Hawks in January 2010.[http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/63843/20100105/hawks_waive_hunter/ Hawks Waive Hunter]{{Dead link|date=April 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. ===Europe=== In 2012, after playing three months with the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague|Ukrainian SuperLeague]] squad [[BC Azovmash|Azovmash Mariupol]],[http://www.asia-basket.com/player.asp?Cntry=CHN&PlayerID=116586&AmNotSure=1 Othello Hunter]. asia-basket.com he signed with the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]] team [[CB Valladolid|Blancos de Rueda Valladolid]].[http://www.cbvalladolid.es/noticias/4/21092012/Blancos-Rueda-incorpora-Othello-Hunter/ Valladolid inks Othello Hunter] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121123201952/http://www.cbvalladolid.es/noticias/4/21092012/Blancos-Rueda-incorpora-Othello-Hunter/ |date=2012-11-23 }}. CB Valladolid On August 26, 2013, Hunter officially signed a one-year deal with the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] team [[Mens Sana Basket|Montepaschi Siena]].{{cite web|last=Caporaso|first=Armando|title=Montepaschi lands Othello Hunter|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/Italy/news/Montepaschi_lands_Othello_Hunter/328465|work=basketball.eurobasket.com|access-date=19 August 2013}}{{cite web|title=MONTEPASCHI SIENA announces Rochestie, Hunter|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/116483/8177/montepaschi-siena-announces-rochestie-hunter|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=26 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219074422/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/116483/8177/montepaschi-siena-announces-rochestie-hunter|archive-date=19 December 2013|url-status=dead}} On July 8, 2014, he signed a contract with the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] team [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]].{{cite news|title=Olympiacos announces Othello Hunter|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/126253/olympiacos-announces-othello-hunter.html|access-date=8 July 2014|work=Sportando.com}} In his first season with the team, in 2014–15, Olympiacos advanced to the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four|2015 Final Four]] of the [[EuroLeague]], where they lost in the [[EuroLeague Finals]] game to the host team [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is Euroleague champion for record ninth time!|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=251&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=16 June 2015|work=euroleague.net}} Olympiacos finished the season winning the [[Greek Basket League 2014-15|2014–15 Greek League]] championship, Hunter's first major title in his career, as they swept their arch rivals [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], in the finals series of the Greek League playoffs. He also won the 2016 Greek League championship with Olympiacos. On August 29, 2016, he signed a two-year deal with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/08/official-announcement-othello-hunter|title=Official announcement: Othello Hunter|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=29 August 2016|access-date=29 August 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/08/this-is-how-othello-hunter-plays|title=This is how Othello Hunter plays|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=29 August 2016|access-date=29 August 2016}} On July 13, 2017, Hunter signed a two-year contract with Russian club [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].{{cite news|title=Othello Hunter joined CSKA|url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=16192&lang=en|access-date=July 13, 2017|work=cskabasket.com|date=July 13, 2017}} On May 23, 2019, Hunter recorded a season-high 22 points, shooting 9-of-10 from the field, along with six rebounds in a 98–82 win over [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]].{{cite news|title=Zenit Saint Petersburg 82 at CSKA Moscow 98|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2019-05-23/Zenit-Saint-Petersburg-at-CSKA-Moscow/334170|access-date=July 16, 2019|work=RealGM.com|date=May 23, 2019}} Hunter went on to win the [[2019 EuroLeague Final Four|2019 EuroLeague championship]] with CSKA. On July 16, 2019, Hunter joined the Israeli team [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], signing a one-year deal with an option for another one.{{cite news|url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9swug73wnjra9slb|title=Maccabi reloads frontline with Hunter|access-date=July 16, 2019|work=EuroLeague.net|date=July 16, 2019}} On December 12, 2019, Hunter recorded a [[EuroLeague]] career-high 20 points, along with seven rebounds in a 90–80 win over his former team [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].{{cite news|title=Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv vs. CSKA Moscow - Game|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=112&seasoncode=E2019|access-date=December 14, 2019|work=EuroLeague.net|date=December 12, 2019}} On February 3, 2020, Hunter signed a 1+1-year contract extension with Maccabi.{{cite news|title=Maccabi extends Othello Hunter's contract |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/maccabi-extends-othello-hunters-contract/|access-date=February 3, 2020|work=Sportando|date=February 3, 2020}} On June 24, 2021, Hunter amicably parted ways with the Israeli club.{{cite news |title=Othello Hunter officially leaves Maccabi Tel Aviv |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/othello-hunter-officially-leaves-maccabi-tel-aviv/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 24, 2021 |date=June 24, 2021 |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} On July 21,
